column1: # The 103 limit-pairs MEASURED THROUGH THE ENGINE - 2026-10-25.
# bucketed them, and closed by saying what was still missing: "Every removal
# still wants what the IOC pair got: the endpoint measured, the candidate keys
# counted against distinct whole records, and the evidence written down before
# the row goes." This file is that measurement.
# EVERY SCHEDULED ROW ON BOTH SIDES OF ALL 103 PAIRS WAS RUN THROUGH THE REAL
# BINARY: 163 rows, serialised one at a time, against one scratch database.
# Serialised rather than parallel because core/hostgate.c paces requests inside
# ONE process and cannot pace several that each think they are alone - ten of
# these rows share api.fda.gov. Run against a PINNED COPY of the binary, which
# earned itself twice over in the same hour: a concurrent session was linking
# bin/japanosint, and an unpinned run exits 126 "Text file busy" and reads as a
# source that returns nothing. 155 of 163 produced a run line.
# THE RULE IS ONE A NUMBER CAN SETTLE, and it refuses wherever the numbers do
#   * the KEEPER is the side that STORES MORE. A row that stores less than its
#     sibling is not the keeper whatever its construct, which is the opposite
#     of resolving this from the declaration - and the declaration was the only
#   * on a tie the hpengine row keeps it, because it declares an identity where
#     VJSON keys on a fixed precedence list - UNLESS it declares no id_keys, in
#     which case retiring the generated row leaves one row with no declared
#     identity, which is rule 4b exposure and not a repair (HOLD_NEEDS_KEY).
#   * on a tie between two rows of the same construct, the fresher cadence
#     keeps it; if the cadences are equal too it is HOLD_TIE, a judgement and
#   * if either side did not run it is HOLD_UNMEASURED. A verdict read off a
#     failed fetch is the mistake this tree keeps catching itself making.
#   RETIRE            67 pairs, of which 63 are actionable (naming 63
#                        distinct rows); the other 4 are the two
#   UNRESOLVED        10   a hand-written collector builds its URL in code
#   HOLD_CYCLES        4   see the cycling-row correction below
# TWO ROWS ARE A KEEPER IN ONE PAIR AND A GONER IN ANOTHER, and that is the one
# structural finding here: gov-pl-sejm-interpellations and nam-mbta-vehicles.
# Both sit in a THREE-row group over one endpoint, where a row can lose to one
# sibling and beat another, so no per-pair verdict can settle it - the group
# needs one keeper chosen across all three. Those two rows and their pairs are
# excluded from any removal built on this file. A pairwise comparison over a
# group of three is not transitive, and reading it as though it were is how a
# repair deletes the row it meant to keep.
# SIX IDS IN THE 2026-10-24 FILE DO NOT EXIST, and the engine said so by name
# 2026-10-25 as the World Bank twin group), gov-hk-legco-bills (main removed it
# three of the four e-Gov/TDnet VJSON rows replaced by EGOV_LAW_LIST_ALL when
# the all-fields-nested finding landed. That is the second inventory this week
# to carry ids that had already been retired with evidence; an inventory is
# dated the moment it is written, so re-resolve its ids before treating any one
# AND THE RULE IS WRONG FOR A CYCLING ROW, WHICH THE MEASUREMENT ITSELF
# EXPOSED - read this before acting on any RETIRE line. "Stores more" is the
# reach of ONE RUN, and a row carrying `page_resume` reads a FURTHER SLICE on
# every run: its one-run total is a per-run figure, not what it reaches. The
# whole BGS cluster is that shape and it is the caveat the 2026-10-24 file had
# already named from the declarations - the generated row asks for more records
# per request than the hp row does. Measured here: geo-bgs-aeromag stores 4,001
# a run against BGS_AEROMAGNETIC_SURVEY's 2,001, so the numeric rule names the
# hp row for retirement - and that hp row CYCLES, so over a cycle it reaches
# the whole collection while the generated row re-reads its first 4,001 for
# ever. Retiring it would be the newest-first-limit error in a new place: a
# bigger per-run number standing in for a complete read.
# So the four BGS pairs are HOLD_CYCLES, not RETIRE. Four of the 69 rows named
# for retirement declare page_resume and all four are those. The remaining 65
# involve no cycling row on either side, so one run IS their reach and the
# WHICH IS WHY NOTHING IS RETIRED ON THIS FILE EITHER. The rule needed patching
# twice in the hour it took to apply it - once for the non-transitive
# three-row groups, once for cycling rows - and a rule that has just been
# wrong twice is not one to run across 65 live sources unreviewed. Everything a
# removal needs is here: the keeper, both sides' measured reading, and the
# Columns: `was` is the 2026-10-24 bucket, `action` the measured verdict,
# stored_a/stored_b what each side actually stored through the engine and
# req_a/req_b how many requests each made (a keeper that pages shows it here).
